faq.body: Transparency is foundational to automotive preservation. Consult our technical clarifications on warranties, exotic paintwork, and custody handoffs.

items.question: What is the difference between polishing and paint correction?
items.answer: Polishing enhances gloss and cleans up light oxidation or hazing. Paint correction is a multi-step compounding process that removes microscopic clearcoat imperfections, permanently eliminating 85% to 95% of swirls, scratches, and etching instead of merely masking them.

items.question: How long does a ceramic coating last?
items.answer: Our ceramic coatings typically last 3 to 5 years depending on the chosen tier, storage conditions, and routine maintenance. Because the coating bonds directly with your vehicle's clearcoat, it provides durable hydrophobic protection and UV resistance throughout its lifespan.

items.question: Do you work on matte or satin finishes and PPF?
items.answer: Yes. Matte, satin finishes, and Paint Protection Film require specific non-abrasive techniques and dedicated coatings that protect surfaces without altering their natural finish or adding unwanted gloss.

items.question: How long will my vehicle be at the studio?
items.answer: Standalone exterior or interior details typically take 4 to 7 hours and are completed same-day. Multi-stage paint correction and ceramic coating packages require 2 to 3 days to allow for precision polishing passes and proper infrared curing before handover.

items.question: How do I maintain my car after detailing?
items.answer: We recommend regular two-bucket hand washes using pH-neutral automotive shampoo, avoiding automated brush car washes, and visiting us for seasonal decontaminating maintenance washes to keep coatings performing optimally.
